question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 5 & -10 \\ -5 & 3 & -10 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Which of the following is a basis of the eigenspace corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2?$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-2.$ So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 5 & -10 \\ -5 & 3 & -10 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & -10 \\ -5 & 5 & -10 \\ 2 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-5{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}-10{x}_{3}=0 \\ -5{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}-10{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & -10 & 0 \\ -5 & 5 & -10 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{2}{5}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & -10 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & -10 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}.$ 

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the required basis is 

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\}.
$$
